ITEM:
<<<
next-image-to-legacy-image: This codemod will safely and automatically rename next/image imports to next/legacy/image to maintain the same behavior as Next.js 12. We recommend running this codemod to quickly update to Next.js 13 automatically.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Migrating shared features / <Image/> Component: Next.js 12 introduced many improvements to the Image Component with a temporary import: next/future/image. These improvements included less client-side JavaScript, easier ways to extend and style images, better accessibility, and native browser lazy loading. Starting in Next.js 13, this new behavior is now the default for next/image. There are two codemods to help you migrate to the new Image Component: next-image-to-legacy-image: This codemod will safely and automatically rename next/image imports to next/legacy/image to maintain the same behavior as Next.js 12. We recommend running this codemod to quickly update to Next.js 13 automatically. next-image-experimental: After running the previous codemod, you can optionally run this experimental codemod to upgrade next/legacy/image to the new next/image, which will remove unused props and add inline styles. Please note this codemod is experimental and only covers static usage (such as <Image src={img} layout="responsive" />) but not dynamic usage (such as <Image {...props} />). Alternatively, you can manually update by following the migration guide and also see the legacy comparison.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 14 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 13 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: next/image default switched to new Image component behavior
paths.description: Starting in Next.js 13, the new Image component behavior (previously available as next/future/image) is the default for next/image. Applications that import next/image and rely on the Next.js 12 behavior will get different behavior after the upgrade unless imports are renamed to next/legacy/image, which the next-image-to-legacy-image codemod does automatically, or the code is migrated to the new component.

conditions.statement: The upgrade from 12 to 14 crosses release 13, where the new next/image behavior became the default.
quotes: Starting in Next.js 13, this new behavior is now the default for next/image.
conditions.relevance: Ties the changed default to release 13, which is crossed by the 12 -> 14 upgrade.

conditions.statement: The application imports next/image and relies on the Next.js 12 behavior of the component.
quotes: rename next/image imports to next/legacy/image to maintain the same behavior as Next.js 12
conditions.relevance: The codemod exists because next/image imports change behavior in Next.js 13 unless renamed to next/legacy/image.
ambiguities: The text does not list which specific props or behaviors break, only that behavior differs from Next.js 12.

conditions.statement: The application already imports from next/legacy/image rather than next/image (for example after running the codemod), so Next.js 12 behavior is preserved.
conditions.relevance: Imports of next/legacy/image keep the Next.js 12 behavior, so the changed default does not apply to those imports.

suggested_actions: Run the next-image-to-legacy-image codemod to rename next/image imports to next/legacy/image and keep the Next.js 12 behavior.

Optionally run the experimental next-image-experimental codemod afterwards to move next/legacy/image to the new next/image; it covers only static usage, not dynamic usage such as <Image {...props} />.
Alternatively, manually migrate to the new next/image by following the migration guide.
